claim: New WHOOP apps start on a Sandbox tier of 10 members.
quote: Every new app starts on the Sandbox tier, which allows up to 10 WHOOP members to connect.

claim: The tiers run 10, 100, 1,000, 5,000 and unlimited.
quote: Sandbox 10 Build 100 Growth 1,000 Scale 5,000 Production Unlimited

claim: Tiers are requested one at a time; from Build onward half the current limit must be connected.
quote: Tiers are earned one at a time. You can only request the tier directly above your current one. From Build onward, moving up requires at least 50% of your current tier's member limit to be connected.

claim: Each request is reviewed by hand.
quote: Requests are reviewed manually, in the order they are received.

claim: Each request needs testing with at least one real member.
quote: Ensure that you have tested your app with at least one WHOOP member.

claim: Each request needs complete app details.
quote: In particular, make sure your App Name , Contact Email(s) , and Privacy Policy URL are filled in and accurate to accelerate the review.

claim: Each request needs adherence to WHOOP's brand guidelines.
quote: Verify your app adheres to the WHOOP Design and Brand Guidelines .

claim: Fitbit / Garmin and table: Garmin's developer program needs Garmin's approval.
quote: After you request access to the Garmin Connect Developer Program and your request has been approved, you will be granted access to the Garmin Developer Portal and can get started on your integration right away.

claim: Fitbit / Garmin: now as Starter and Enterprise Access.
quote: Starter Access: Developers can gain immediate access and launch with Garmin, with access to core data and tools.

claim: Fitbit / Garmin: now as Starter and Enterprise Access.
quote: Enterprise Access: For companies operating at scale, this new model aligns with growth, offering expanded data access, reliability, and enterprise-grade support.

claim: Fitbit / Garmin and table: some features are marked Supported with Enterprise Access only.
quote: Supported with Enterprise Access only

claim: Why teams look: WHOOP's developer overview requires a WHOOP membership to develop an app.
quote: You must have a WHOOP membership to develop an app on the Developer Platform.

claim: Why teams look: the people you read data from are WHOOP members who grant consent with their own accounts.
quote: you can use the OAuth standard to request consent from WHOOP members to access data on their behalf.

claim: Why teams look: WHOOP's developer site bundles the strap with the membership; its one-month trial includes Peak membership and 5.0 hardware.
quote: Try WHOOP free for 1 month. Trial includes Peak membership, 5.0 hardware, Onyx SuperKnit band, battery pack, and more.

claim: Junction says it supports 300+ devices.
quote: We currently support 300+ devices.

claim: ROOK says 400+ wearables and health data sources.
quote: ROOK is a single integration for 400+ wearables and health data sources that supports all major wearable providers, with more being added every day.

claim: Terra lists WHOOP among the integrations that need your own credentials from the integration's developer portal.
quote: Required integrations need your own credentials, created in the integration's developer portal and added to your Terra dashboard before end users can connect.

claim: Terra's table marks WHOOP as Required.
quote: Whoop WHOOP Event-Driven Required

claim: Junction calls WHOOP a bring-your-own-OAuth-only provider: you need your own app in WHOOP's developer dashboard.
quote: WHOOP is a BYOO only provider, so you will need your own app in WHOOP’s developer dashboard

claim: Junction repeats WHOOP's 10-member development limit.
quote: Apps can be used for development immediately with a limit of 10 WHOOP members.

claim: ROOK says clients must create their own WHOOP developer accounts.
quote: To integrate with Dexcom , Samsung Health , Strava and Whoop , clients are required to create their own developer accounts with these providers.

claim: Terra's Quick Start plan starts at $499 a month.
quote: From $499 / month

claim: Terra's Quick Start plan includes 100,000 API credits.
quote: Includes 100,000 Unified API credits

claim: Junction's Launch plan is $300 a month for up to 500 connected users.
quote: Start on Launch if you are connecting wearables and devices for up to 500 users — it covers the Link widget, 300+ device integrations, and usage analytics for a flat $300 a month.

claim: Junction's Launch plan covers 1 to 500 connected users.
quote: Launch covers 1-500 connected users.

claim: ROOK's Core plan is $399 a month.
quote: $399 USD per month

claim: ROOK's Core plan covers up to 750 active users.
quote: Up to 750 active users

claim: Junction (formerly Vital): Vital renamed itself Junction.
quote: Vital was always about helping healthcare systems operate more effectively.

claim: The legacy token endpoint now answers that the endpoints were decommissioned on October 30, 2026 (HTTP 410, read 2026-11-18 through source-snapshot).
quote: The legacy Fitbit Web API and OAuth 2.0 endpoints were decommissioned on October 30, 2026.

claim: Google's pages give November 2, 2026 as the legacy Fitbit Web API's turn-off.
quote: November 2, 2026 (API turn-off): The Fitbit Web API and Fitbit OAuth endpoints will be turned off and will no longer function or sync data to or from Fitbit users.

claim: Google says existing access and refresh tokens cannot be transferred, so users re-consent.
quote: existing access and refresh tokens cannot be transferred, requiring users to re-consent to your updated integration.

claim: Oura has its own 10-user cap until it approves your app.
quote: By default, API Applications have a ten user limit. If you want to release your application to a wider audience, your application needs to be approved.
